newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Mir crew told to choose module; repair kit ready.
newsitem.headline: Mir crew told to choose module; repair kit ready.

text.p: Mission control on Monday told a Russian-American space crew preparing to repair the damaged Mir space station to get ready for training and choose a site for it aboard the vessel.
Russian experts had prepared all the equipment needed for repairs to Mir's power supply and would ship it to the Baikonur launch pad later on Monday, a senior space official said.
Reporters heard a radio exchange in which the deputy head of the mission, Vladimir Solovyov, told the cosmonauts to choose a module of the Mir for training in spacesuits.
"You have to concentrate on physical exercise, diet and have to drink at least two litres of water a day," a doctor said during the morning radio contact.
A mission control spokeswoman said the three men -- two Russian cosmonauts and a British-born American astronaut -- had spent a peaceful night.
"Medical equipment showed no divergence from the norm," she told Reuters.
The crew looked well and confident on Sunday in their first television link with Earth since their accident in orbit last Wednesday. All three were smiling and looked fit.

Mir lost between 30 and 40 percent of its electric power potential after colliding with the cargo craft during a manual docking manoeuvre. The Spektr scientific module, which was already docked with Mir, was holed during the collision.
The crew on Mir face risky repair work. The Russians will don spacesuits to enter Spektr while U.S. astronaut Michael Foale sits in the escape capsule for safety.
Solovyov told reporters the Progress cargo craft containing the necessary repair equipment was due to be launched from Baikonur on July 5 and dock with Mir two days later.

He said 20 electric cables, hermetic electric connections and a specially-devised "hermoplate" needed for station power-supply repairs would be flown to Baikonur, in the steppes of Kazakhstan, later on Monday.
Solovyov said the crew would leave the job of sealing the hole in the Spektr science module to a fresh team.
"This crew has not been trained to do this kind of repairs (sealing). The work is really difficult," he said. "Hermetic sealing will be done by a new crew, due to replace this one in August."
